canonical_name: Bochner's theorem (characteristic-function form on the real line)
canonical_statement: A function phi : Real -> Complex is the characteristic function of a Borel probability measure on Real if and only if phi is continuous, phi(0) = 1, and phi is positive definite: for every n, points t_1,...,t_n in Real, and coefficients c_1,...,c_n in Complex, the sum over j,k of c_j times conjugate(c_k) times phi(t_j-t_k) is a nonnegative real number.
domain_and_universes: phi : Real -> Complex; finite index types in universe 0; Borel probability measure mu on Real
hypotheses: phi is positive definite for all finite point and coefficient families
conclusion: There exists a Borel probability measure mu on Real whose Fourier/characteristic transform equals phi at every real argument; conversely every such transform has the three stated properties.
excluded_claims: locally compact abelian groups beyond Real
degenerate_and_boundary_cases: the empty finite family gives the zero quadratic sum
the singleton family and phi(0)=1 enforce the normalized diagonal
the zero-frequency transform equals total mass
Fourier sign conventions require checked reflection/conjugation transport

alternate_encodings.target: continuity only at zero plus positive definiteness
finite lists/matrices rather than finite index types
